current.text: Category experts rank him around 6th to 10th. Most would take him at pick 6 or 7, not at pick 5, and some put Giannis, Jayson Tatum, Anthony Edwards or Kawhi Leonard ahead of him.
At pick 5 he is a mild bust in category leagues. Taking him anywhere from pick 5 to 8 neither wins nor loses a league.
Experts rate him higher in points leagues, where he could finish ahead of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, than in categories.
He often falls in drafts. In one mock he fell to pick 9.
In an auction mock he went for 48 USD.
Josh would pay no more than 45 USD for him. Another expert puts his value at about 50 USD and says he can go for around 35 USD if he is nominated early.
Detroit has very few creators besides him. The team lost Tobias Harris's creation.
His usage may rise after the roster changes, but a bigger creation load with little help around him could hurt his efficiency.
Detroit wants him to take more catch-and-shoot threes, with Ausar Thompson running some of the offense.
If the plan with Ausar Thompson and Jalen Duren on the ball is failing by January, Detroit may trade for a secondary playmaker at the deadline.
Last season he led the group in potential assists (24.7 per 100), so there is room for more. His assists could go over 10 per game.
Experts want his free throw percentage back over 85%. Last season's drop worries them.
He is healthy now. Detroit has no notable injuries.
Detroit plays 4, 3 and 4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. The team has 15 back-to-backs, and no rest risk is expected.
Detroit is projected to win 50 to 51 games and be the third or fourth seed in the East.

durable.text: Assists are his standout category, far above the top 250 pool. Points and steals are also clearly above average.
His turnovers are high. That is a clear weakness in the TO category.
For a top pick, his FG% and FT% are only middling. Experts call his efficiency iffy.
He carries a heavy creation load, which hurts his finishing and his two-point percentage.
He has a spotty injury history. He had a punctured lung at the end of last season and some lower-body problems in recent years.
One expert is not particularly worried about his injury history.
Detroit is built on defense. The front office wants only enough offense, which leaves little creation around him.

tags.name: sites disagree on price
tags.detail: Yahoo rank 5 and 65.2 USD average cost; ESPN rank 11 and 57.2 USD

note: Assists win him the most value, but his turnovers cost the most. That makes him a natural fit for a punt TO build, while his FG% and FT% are only middling for a first-rounder. The Yahoo average cost of 65.2 USD is well above both his Yahoo value of 57 USD and the experts' price. The experts rank him 6th to 10th in categories and cap him at about 45 to 50 USD, close to the 55 USD our league paid last season. So let others pay the Yahoo price. Early in the season, check whether his FT% gets back toward 85%, whether his efficiency holds with so little creation around him, and whether his assists go over 10.
